scope: Read-only exact candidate production code and original runner/rows. No build, benchmark, source or runner mutation. Existing negative results unchanged.
verdict: No source evidence of expensive compile-owned response-after-drop or detached compile cleanup. Existing first-noop regression is already inside current driver/resident timers, so a previous response cleanup queued before current compile cannot explain that observed gap.

ownership_evidence.finding: let report receives a String from session.compile_path(...).to_json(). The temporary CompileReport, current CompileOptions and path are destroyed by the end of the let statement, before elapsed is captured and before writeln. The report String drops at compile match-arm exit, before the explicit output.flush. Retained CompilationSession deliberately survives the request; it is not queued for asynchronous cleanup.

function_checkpoint is a local of compile_project_request. Its final Arc/drop cleanup and trim_history finish before the function returns to compile_project_path, hence before serialization. The outer project/source locals drop on compile_project_path return, also before resident writes any response. report.seconds can precede the outer function final local drops, but resident.elapsed_ms and external wall include those drops.

Verified value, lowering view, LLVM text, native build/publication guards and per-call typed Arc references are local to finish_typed and end before its return. CompileReport contains diagnostics/path maps/commands/object receipt strings/interfaces/events, no LLVM handle, typed module or FunctionSession checkpoint. It is converted to String and destroyed before output.

Codegen and parallel-lowering workers are scoped and explicitly joined, including panic/error paths. Native linker/compiler uses Command::output(), which waits for completion. Build staging destructor synchronously removes its directory before returning. No detached cleanup worker in this path.

LLVM Context/Module/Machine/Layout/PassOptions/Buffer are private synchronous RAII locals of compile_input; returned Object contains copied bytes and receipt only. Disposal occurs before compile_input returns to its joined worker. Receipt.total_ns is evaluated before those RAII drops, so object subtotals can omit disposal while resident request total includes it.
NativePublication rollback and Staging remove_dir_all are synchronous local guard destructors, not response-after tasks.

boundary_caveats.finding: stdout is line buffered in actual run. The newline may become readable during writeln, before the explicit flush and the report String drop. Thus receipt of newline is not a formal loop-ready barrier. Only the serialization String, tiny command line and bookkeeping remain on this inspected path; no deferred huge CFG/LLVM owner identified.
boundary_caveats.impact: Do not claim a strict fully-quiescent endpoint from newline alone; also do not inflate this small formal gap into an established 90-180ms cause.

boundary_caveats.finding: Worker.read_json returns after Python json.loads, so external wall already includes client JSON parsing. CPU after snapshot is taken after sampling thread join, slightly later than wall endpoint. Existing external-minus-resident is about submillisecond to a few milliseconds for the inspected requests.
boundary_caveats.impact: Current external wall is compilation plus transport/client decoding; CPU and wall endpoints are not exactly identical.

boundary_caveats.finding: Source proves joins for explicit ZIL worker/subprocess paths, not arbitrary hidden threads or asynchronous OS writeback within opaque LLVM/libc/kernel implementations. No evidence for those as this regression cause.
boundary_caveats.impact: Do not promise system-wide quiescence, disk fsync durability or zero background OS work.

minimal_symmetric_boundary_probe.necessity: Optional formal boundary diagnostic, not a required correction of the proven compilation cleanup interval and not a new performance explanation. Preserve original metric and raw runs.
minimal_symmetric_boundary_probe.protocol:
For every existing compile, including named-parent preparations and errors, send compile
stats
 together under the same start timer. Read and retain the compile response, recording the legacy response wall endpoint; immediately read the stats response and record compile-plus-barrier wall endpoint. Take final CPU and stop RSS sampler only after the stats acknowledgement. No sleep, no additional compile, no extra warm request, no cache reset.
minimal_symmetric_boundary_probe.validation: Stats requests must equal just-completed compile number; active_queries=0, same expected epoch, no unexpected reset; archive both responses, both wall endpoints and the CPU-boundary label. Stats processing proves the preceding compile arm has exited and flush/loop progression has completed. It does not establish arbitrary native-library background-thread quiescence.
minimal_symmetric_boundary_probe.fairness: Identical protocol for both arms, all requests and both modes; barrier overhead remains inside extended wall/CPU and is never subtracted. Keep original complete-response wall separately. Do not silently compare new barrier total to old headline totals or redefine fixed user timing; explicitly version/label the diagnostic boundary.
minimal_symmetric_boundary_probe.after_probe: Root planned both modes x four blocks x all original nine requests remains appropriate. This review withdraws any need to reduce user-prescribed scenario coverage. A significant barrier delta would be new evidence requiring investigation; absent it, retain the original complete-response boundary and diagnose inside the timed driver.

merge_status: Unchanged: unresolved negative signal still requires repeated matched measurement; response-after-cleanup hypothesis is unsupported and cannot justify merge.
